description: A full week for an IC engineer with three genuine pending items of wildly different stakes. The trivial ones are loud (repeated, chatty, multiple reminders) and the consequential one — a compliance-gated dependency patch with a hard Friday deadline — is stated once, quietly. Surfacing all three but ranking the survey above the patch is a poor-ranking failure even though recall is perfect.

events.text: @kiran-vasquez you're one of four people who haven't filled in the developer-tooling survey. It's 6 questions, takes 3 minutes. Please do it this week.
Survey nudge #2 — still waiting on Kiran, Mika and two others. I will keep posting this daily, sorry.

events.context_label: Patch required: crypto-utils 2.x — service owners must merge by Friday 24th
events.text: Kiran — you are listed as the owner of the ledger-api service, which pins crypto-utils 2.4.1. The advisory is exploitable via the signature-verification path, which ledger-api uses. Patched release is 2.4.9. Our SOC 2 window closes Friday the 24th; any service still on an affected version after that goes on the exception register and I have to file a written deviation with your name on it. You are the only person who can merge for ledger-api.
@kiran-vasquez do you want the August 6th or August 13th slot for your retry-semantics talk? Either works, I just need to put a name in the calendar.
Bumping — August 6 or August 13? Genuinely no wrong answer, I'll take a coin flip if you'd rather.
Survey nudge #3. Two left. You know who you are.
Heads up, I bumped crypto-utils in payments-api and the only breaking change was the return type on verifyDetached. Ten-minute fix if anyone else is on 2.4.x.

Tell Mika whether you want the August 6th or August 13th brown-bag slot so it can go in the calendar.
Fill in the six-question developer-tooling survey.

ground_truth.notes: Recall is easy here; ranking is the whole test. The survey generates three messages and the brown-bag two, while the patch is a single email — so message count, mention count and recency all point the wrong way. AC-7 asks for top-3 relevance: all three items belong in the briefing, but the patch must be first. A briefing that opens with the survey, or that mentions the patch only after both trivia items, fails this fixture even with perfect recall, precision and citations. Ravi's message is not a pending item — it is context that makes the real item cheaper to act on, and a good briefing attaches it to the patch item rather than listing it separately.
